abstract_en: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. abstract_es: Abstract

En pacientes con sospecha de infarto de miocardio, la vía 0/1 h (retiradas de sangre a 0 h y 1 h) se recomienda en las directrices actuales para la estratificación temprana del riesgo. Sin embargo, los ensayos individuales utilizaron diferentes resultados de seguridad, y los resultados de eficacia no fueron concluyentes o no se evaluaron. Realizamos una revisión sistemática y un metaanálisis individual de los datos de los participantes de todos los ensayos controlados aleatorizados para sintetizar la totalidad de la evidencia, evaluar la heterogeneidad entre los ensayos y evaluar los resultados clínicamente relevantes utilizando definiciones armonizadas en todos los ensayos. En esta revisión sistemática y metaanálisis de datos de participantes individuales, se buscó PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform desde el inicio hasta el 6 de julio de 2026, sin restricciones lingüísticas, para ensayos aleatorizados que comparan la seguridad y eficacia de las vías 0/1 h versus 0/3 h (tiradas de sangre a 0 h y 3 h, es decir, atención estándar).Se obtuvieron datos de participantes individuales y se armonizaron las definiciones de resultados. Tras la recepción de los datos de cada participante, pero antes de la armonización o el análisis de los datos, el resultado primario de seguridad se perfeccionó en un compuesto de muerte por cualquier causa o nuevo infarto de miocardio tipo 1 en un plazo de 30 días, a partir del compuesto original especificado de muerte por cualquier causa o cualquier nuevo infarto de miocardio. Los resultados primarios de eficacia fueron la duración de la estancia en el departamento de emergencia y el alta directa del departamento de emergencia. Entre ellos, la definición de los resultados primarios de seguridad varió, y en cuatro ensayos no se notificó la duración de la estancia del departamento de urgencias para toda la población de análisis, incluyendo 110 933 presentaciones de pacientes (55 489 manejadas con la vía 0/1 h y 55 444 manejadas con la vía 0/3 h). En 30 días, se produjo muerte por cualquier causa o infarto de miocardio nuevo tipo 1 en 446 presentaciones de pacientes (0·8%) con la vía 0/1 h versus 562 presentaciones de pacientes (1·0%) con la vía 0/3 h (proporción de odds agrupados de efectos aleatorios [OR] 0·83 [IC 95% 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; La duración de la estancia del departamento de emergencia fue de 314 min (IQR 211-481) en el grupo de vía de 0/1 h frente a 308 min (209-453) en el grupo de vía de 0/3 h (proporción media geométrica agrupada de efectos aleatorios 1·03 [IC 95% 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; En promedio, las pruebas de troponina cardíacas anteriores no redujeron la duración de la estancia en el departamento de urgencias ni aumentaron claramente el alta directa, y la heterogeneidad sustancial entre los estudios indica que los efectos del tratamiento podrían no traducirse de manera uniforme en todos los sistemas de atención de la salud.Para los hospitales que consideren la transición de una vía de 0/3 h a una vía de 0/1 h, las decisiones de implementación deben tener en cuenta consideraciones de diagnóstico y organización más amplias.

short: Empagliflozin's role in cardiometabolic disease treatment: an Egyptian expert's view.

abstract_en: Given the expanding therapeutic indications of empagliflozin (EMPA) beyond glycemic control and the growing burden of cardiometabolic diseases, this review evaluated its efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness in the Egyptian population within the global context. A comprehensive literature review of PubMed and Google Scholar identified clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical guidelines published in English up to July 2025. We included studies reporting EMPA's pharmacological profile, mechanisms of action, and clinical outcomes on diabetes mellitus, cardiometabolic diseases, renal and hepatic functions, safety during Ramadan fasting, and cost-effectiveness. EMPA, as monotherapy or combination therapy, improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes through Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibition. For type 1 diabetes mellitus, despite improving glycemic control as an adjunct therapy, it is not recommended due to the increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis. EMPA reduces major cardiovascular events, heart failure hospitalization, and chronic kidney disease progression, with modest weight loss and blood pressure reduction, in patients with or without diabetes. Emerging evidence suggests benefits in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), although it is not approved for this indication. EMPA demonstrates a favorable safety profile and low hypoglycemia risk during Ramadan fasting. It enhances patients' quality of life and is considered cost-effective. EMPA extends beyond glucose-lowering by reducing cardiorenal morbidity and mortality in patients with or without diabetes. It shows a favorable safety profile, even during Ramadan fasting, supporting its suitability for the large Muslim population. Further research should evaluate its role in MASLD and assess cost-effectiveness in Egypt.
abstract_es: Abstract

Dada la expansión de las indicaciones terapéuticas de empagliflozina (EMPA) más allá del control glucémico y la creciente carga de enfermedades cardiometabólicas, esta revisión evaluó su eficacia, seguridad y rentabilidad en la población egipcia dentro del contexto global. Una revisión completa de la literatura de PubMed y Google Scholar identificó ensayos clínicos, revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis y directrices clínicas publicadas en inglés hasta julio de 2025. Incluyemos estudios que reportan el perfil farmacológico de EMPA, mecanismos de acción y resultados clínicos sobre diabetes mellitus, enfermedades cardiometabólicas, funciones renales y hepáticas, seguridad durante el ayuno Ramadán y rentabilidad. La EMPA, en monoterapia o terapia combinada, mejora el control glucémico en diabetes tipo 2 a través de la inhibición del cotransportador de sodio-glucosa-2 (SGLT-2). Para la diabetes mellitus tipo 1, a pesar de mejorar el control glucémico como terapia concomitante, no se recomienda debido al aumento del riesgo de cetoacidosis diabética. La EMPA reduce los eventos cardiovasculares mayores, la hospitalización por insuficiencia cardiaca y la progresión de la enfermedad renal crónica, con una modesta pérdida de peso y reducción de la presión arterial, en pacientes con o sin diabetes. La EMPA demuestra un perfil de seguridad favorable y bajo riesgo de hipoglucemia durante el ayuno de Ramadán. Mejora la calidad de vida de los pacientes y se considera rentable. La EMPA se extiende más allá de la reducción de la glucosa al reducir la morbilidad y mortalidad cardiorrenales en pacientes con o sin diabetes. Muestra un perfil de seguridad favorable, incluso durante el ayuno de Ramadán, apoyando su idoneidad para la gran población musulmana.

title: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
short: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
summary: La eficacia y seguridad comparativas de los nuevos fármacos (incluyendo inhibidores del cotransportador de sodio-glucosa-2 [SGLT-2Is], agonistas del receptor péptido-1 similar al glucagón [GLP-1RAs], antagonistas de los receptores mineralocorticoides no esteroideos [nsMRAs] y estimuladores solubles de guanilato ciclasa [sGCs]) para la insuficiencia cardíaca con fracción de eyección levemente reducida o conservada (HFmrEF/HFpEF) permanece en gran medida sin ser clara. Realizamos una revisión sistemática y un metaanálisis de red para evaluar sus efectos comparativos sobre la ICmrEF/HFpEF, con el objetivo de proporcionar una guía basada en pruebas para la selección del tratamiento.

abstract_en: The comparative efficacy and safety of the new drugs (including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT-2Is], glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RAs], non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [nsMRAs], and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators [sGCs]) for heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved (HFmrEF/HFpEF) ejection fraction remains largely unclear. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate their comparative effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for treatment selection. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were comprehensively searched. We included randomized controlled trials that compared nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA with placebo for patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Primary efficacy outcomes were cardiovascular (CV) death, hospitalization for heart failure (HF hospitalization), and all-cause mortality, while primary safety outcomes were adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs). The main analysis was conducted to compare the effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF between individual drugs. A frequentist network meta-analysis with random-effects models was used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. A total of 20 randomized controlled trials (RCTs, including 10 drugs from 35 publications) were included for analyses, but none provided head-to-head direct comparisons. No significant differences among all the individual drugs were found in risks of CV death or all-cause mortality. Compared with exenatide, low or moderate certainty evidence showed that dapagliflozin (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36-0.91), empagliflozin (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86), and semaglutide (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20-0.91) were related to decreased risk of HF hospitalization. No significant differences in the risk of SAEs were found among the individual drugs. Compared with empagliflozin, very low certainty evidence showed that tirzepatide (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32) was related to increased risk of AEs. When comparing the four drug classes (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA), no significant differences in efficacy outcomes were found, while SGLT-2I (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.96) was associated with a decreased risk of AEs compared with GLP-1RA. No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF. PROSPERO identifier number CRD420251143542.
abstract_es: Abstract

La eficacia y seguridad comparativas de los nuevos fármacos (incluyendo inhibidores del cotransportador de sodio-glucosa-2 [SGLT-2Is], agonistas del receptor péptido-1 similar al glucagón [GLP-1RAs], antagonistas de los receptores mineralocorticoides no esteroideos [nsMRAs] y estimuladores solubles de guanilato ciclasa [sGCs]) para la insuficiencia cardíaca con fracción de eyección levemente reducida o conservada (HFmrEF/HFpEF) permanece en gran medida sin ser clara. Realizamos una revisión sistemática y un metaanálisis de red para evaluar sus efectos comparativos sobre la ICmrEF/HFpEF, con el objetivo de proporcionar una guía basada en pruebas para la selección del tratamiento. Se incluyeron ensayos aleatorizados controlados que compararon nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I y GLP-1RA con placebo para pacientes con ICmrEF/HFpEF. Los resultados primarios de eficacia fueron muerte cardiovascular (CV), hospitalización por insuficiencia cardiaca (hospitalización por IC) y mortalidad por cualquier causa, mientras que los resultados primarios de seguridad fueron eventos adversos (AE) y eventos adversos graves (EAE). El análisis principal se llevó a cabo para comparar los efectos sobre ICmrEF/HFpEF entre medicamentos individuales.Se utilizó un metaanálisis de red frecuente con modelos de efectos aleatorios para calcular las ratios de riesgo (RR) para los resultados dicotómicos y diferencias medias estandarizadas (SMD) para los resultados continuos. Para los análisis se incluyeron un total de 20 ensayos aleatorizados controlados (RCTs, incluyendo 10 fármacos de 35 publicaciones), pero ninguno proporcionó comparaciones directas cabeza a cabeza; no se encontraron diferencias significativas entre todos los fármacos individuales en el riesgo de muerte CV o mortalidad por cualquier causa; en comparación con exenatida, evidencia de certeza baja o moderada mostró que dapagliflozina (RR 0,57, IC 95% 0,36-0,91), empagliflozina (RR 0,54, IC 95% 0,34-0,86) y semaglutida (RR 0,43, IC 95% 0,20-0,91) estaban relacionadas con la disminución del riesgo de hospitalización por IC; no se encontraron diferencias significativas en el riesgo de EAE entre los fármacos individuales. En comparación con empagliflozina, la evidencia de seguridad muy baja mostró que la tirzepatida (RR 1,17, IC 95% 1,04-1,32) estaba relacionada con el aumento del riesgo de EA. Al comparar las cuatro clases de fármacos (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I y GLP-1RA), no se encontraron diferencias significativas en los resultados de eficacia, mientras que SGLT-2I (RR 0,87, IC 95% 0,78-0,96) se asociaron con una disminución del riesgo de EA en comparación con GLP-1RA. No se encontraron diferencias significativas entre los individuos SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA y fármacos SGC en riesgo de muerte CV, mortalidad por cualquier causa o EAE en pacientes con ICFMrEF/HFpEF. abstract_en: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior ischemic stroke represent a high-risk population facing competing risks of recurrent thromboembolism and hemorrhagic complications. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended over vitamin K antagonists for stroke prevention in AF, no randomized controlled clinical trial has directly compared individual DOACs to each other in this population. We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled clinical trials enrolling patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary outcome was any stroke. Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. The evidence network comprised 6 trials (18 395 patients) in a star-shaped structure. Each DOAC was informed by a single warfarin-controlled trial, and 2 trials used aspirin as the comparator. All between-DOAC comparisons were indirect. In the network meta-analysis, compared with warfarin, apixaban was the only agent to significantly reduce both any stroke (RR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.53-0.97]) and major bleeding (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]). Dabigatran, apixaban, and edoxaban each significantly reduced hemorrhagic stroke and ICH versus warfarin, whereas rivaroxaban did not reach significance for any bleeding outcome. Edoxaban was the only agent associated with significantly lower cardiovascular (RR, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]) and all-cause mortality (RR, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.72-0.99]). Based on indirect comparisons only, no differences between individual DOACs were observed. In patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke, individual DOACs reduced intracranial and systemic bleeding relative to warfarin, although not uniformly across agents. Apixaban alone significantly reduced both any stroke and major bleeding versus warfarin, but differences between individual DOACs could not be established given the small number of trials. Los pacientes con fibrilación auricular (FA) y ictus isquémico previo representan una población de alto riesgo que enfrenta riesgos de tromboembolismo recurrente y complicaciones hemorrágicas.Aunque se recomiendan anticoagulantes orales directos (DOAC) sobre antagonistas de la vitamina K para la prevención de ictus en FA, ningún ensayo clínico controlado aleatorizado ha comparado directamente los DOAC individuales entre sí en esta población. Realizamos una revisión sistemática y un metaanálisis frecuente de la red de efectos aleatorios de ensayos clínicos aleatorizados controlados que inscriban pacientes con FA y ictus isquémico previo o ataque isquémico transitorio. El resultado primario fue cualquier accidente cerebrovascular.Los resultados secundarios incluyeron ictus isquémico, ictus hemorrágico, hemorragia mayor, hemorragia intracraneal (ICH), mortalidad cardiovascular y mortalidad por cualquier causa.Los efectos del tratamiento se expresaron como coeficientes de riesgo (RR) con IC 95%.La red de evidencia incluyó 6 ensayos (18 395 pacientes) en una estructura en forma de estrella.Cada DOAC fue informado por un solo ensayo controlado por warfarina, y 2 ensayos utilizaron aspirina como comparador. Todas las comparaciones entre DOAC fueron indirectas. En el metaanálisis de la red, comparado con warfarina, apixaban fue el único agente que redujo significativamente tanto cualquier ictus (RR, 0,72 [IC 95%, 0,53-0,97]) como hemorragia mayor (RR, 0,73 [IC 95%, 0,54-0,99]). Dabigatrán, apixaban y edoxaban cada uno redujeron significativamente el ictus hemorrágico y la IC frente a warfarina, mientras que rivaroxaban no alcanzó significación para ningún resultado hemorrágico. Edoxaban fue el único agente asociado con una disminución significativa de las cardiovasculares (RR, 0,79 [IC 95%, 0,65-0,97]) y mortalidad por cualquier causa (RR, 0,84 [IC 95%, 0,72-0,99)]. En pacientes con FA y ictus isquémico previo, los DOAC individuales redujeron el sangrado intracraneal y sistémico en relación con la warfarina, aunque no de manera uniforme entre los agentes. Apixaban solo redujo significativamente tanto cualquier ictus como hemorragia mayor frente a warfarina, pero no se pudieron establecer diferencias entre los DOAC individuales dado el pequeño número de ensayos. abstract_en: Atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery is common and is associated with stroke, prolonged hospitalization, and mortality; yet, the optimal oral anticoagulant in this setting remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) in adults requiring oral anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was any bleeding; secondary outcomes were stroke or transient ischemic attack, systemic embolism, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, reoperation, and length of hospital stay. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) were pooled with random-effects models, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Five randomized trials including 302 patients (153 DOACs and 149 warfarin) were included; rivaroxaban was tested in 3 trials, and apixaban and dabigatran in 1 trial each. Any bleeding did not differ significantly between DOACs and VKAs (9.2% vs 8.1%; OR, 1.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-3.99).

abstract_en: Concomitant coronary artery disease affects 40-75% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Three recent randomized trials yielded conflicting findings: NOTION-3 demonstrated reduced composite events with pre-TAVI percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PRO-TAVI showed non-inferiority of PCI deferral with less bleeding; neither demonstrated mortality benefit. No previous meta-analysis combined all 3 trials with observational evidence, applied design-stratified GRADE certainty, or explored cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (3 randomized trials, 13 observational cohorts; 8,207 patients). Ten prespecified outcomes were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); 30-day all-cause mortality was primary. GRADE certainty was assessed separately for randomized and observational evidence. Prespecified design-based subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Pre-TAVI PCI was not associated with significant differences in 30-day all-cause mortality (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.90-1.77; I2 = 32%) or 1-year mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15; I2 = 0%). Major bleeding (RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.98-1.44) and major vascular complications (RR 1.48, 95% CI 0.95-2.30) showed borderline non-significant trends favoring PCI deferral (both I2 = 0%). Excluding Griese et al. 2014, the principal driver of harm and heterogeneity, reduced cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity (RR 0.91; I2 = 24%). No significant differences occurred in stroke, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, pacemaker implantation, or rehospitalization. Routine pre-TAVI PCI confers no mortality benefit and may increase bleeding and vascular complications; PCI should be individualized according to coronary complexity, lesion significance, and bleeding risk.

La enfermedad coronaria concomitante afecta al 40-75% de los pacientes sometidos a implante valvular aórtico transcatéter (TAVI).Tres ensayos aleatorizados recientes arrojaron hallazgos contradictorios: NOTION-3 demostró reducción de eventos compuestos con intervención coronaria percutánea pre-TAVI (IPC), mientras que PRO-TAVI mostró no inferioridad de postergación de ICP con menor sangrado; ninguno demostró beneficio de mortalidad. Ningún metaanálisis previo combinó los 3 ensayos con evidencia observacional, certeza GRADE estratificada por diseño aplicado o heterogeneidad de mortalidad cardiovascular explorada. Se realizó una revisión sistemática y meta-análisis de 16 estudios (3 ensayos aleatorizados, 13 cohortes observacionales; 8.207 pacientes); se agruparon diez resultados preespecificados con relación al riesgo de efectos aleatorios de Mantel-Haenszel (RR) con intervalos de confianza del 95% (IC); la mortalidad por todas las causas de 30 días fue primaria; la certeza GRADE se evaluó por separado para evidencia aleatoria y observacional; se realizaron subgrupos basados en diseño preespecificados y análisis de sensibilidad de una sola salida; la ICP pre-TAVI no se asoció con diferencias significativas en mortalidad por todas las causas de 30 días (RR 1,26, IC 95% 0,90-1,77; I2 = 32%) o mortalidad a 1 año (RR 1,00, IC 95% 0,87-1,15; I2 = 0%). Las hemorragias mayores (RR 1,19, IC 95% 0,98-1,44) y las complicaciones vasculares mayores (RR 1,48, IC 95% 0,95-2,30) mostraron tendencias no significativas límites que favorecen el aplazamiento de la ICP (ambos I2 = 0%). Excluyendo Griese et al. 2014, el principal motor de daño y heterogeneidad, reducción de la heterogeneidad de la mortalidad cardiovascular (RR 0,91; I2 = 24%). No hubo diferencias significativas en el accidente cerebrovascular, infarto de miocardio, lesión renal aguda, implantación de marcapasos o rehospitalización.

abstract_en: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) in preterm infants results from impaired pulmonary vascular development and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Diuretics are commonly used to reduce pulmonary vascular congestion and improve oxygenation, but their efficacy and safety remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of diuretic use in preterm infants with BPD-PH. Primary outcomes were mortality and need for home respiratory support; secondary outcomes were echocardiographic and clinical parameters, and adverse effects such as hyponatremia, nephrocalcinosis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to October 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSI) evaluating diuretics in preterm infants (< 32 weeks' gestation) with BPD-PH diagnosed by echocardiography at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (ROBINS-I). Outcomes were synthesized narratively, and a meta-analysis was performed where sufficient data were available. Of 492 studies identified, 2 NRSI (n = 49) met inclusion criteria, both were at serious risk of bias. No RCTs exist on diuretics for BPD-PH in preterm infants. Mortality, respiratory, discharge outcomes and adverse effects were reported inconsistently. Meta-analysis of limited data demonstrated small improvements in echocardiographic markers, but the certainty of evidence was very low due to heterogeneity between the two included studies. To conclude, evidence supporting the use of diuretics in BPD-PH in preterm infants remains limited and of low certainty. High quality studies are needed to better define their safety and efficacy.

La displasia broncopulmonar asociada a hipertensión pulmonar (HPP-BPD) en bebés prematuros resulta del deterioro del desarrollo vascular pulmonar y contribuye significativamente a la morbilidad y mortalidad. Los diuréticos se utilizan comúnmente para reducir la congestión vascular pulmonar y mejorar la oxigenación, pero su eficacia y seguridad permanecen sin ser claras. Esta revisión sistemática tuvo como objetivo evaluar la eficacia y seguridad del uso de diuréticos en bebés prematuros con HPP-B. Los principales resultados fueron mortalidad y necesidad de apoyo respiratorio en el hogar; los resultados secundarios fueron ecocardiográficos y clínicos, y efectos adversos como hiponatremia, nefrocalcinosis. Se buscaron MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central y ClinicalTrials.gov desde el inicio hasta octubre de 2025. Se incluyeron ensayos aleatorizados controlados (RCT) y estudios no aleatorizados de intervenciones (NRSI) que evaluaron diuréticos en lactantes prematuros (< 32 semanas de gestación) con PAB-PH diagnosticados por ecocardiografía a las 36 semanas de edad postmenstrual. Dos revisores realizaron independientemente la extracción de datos y la evaluación del riesgo de bias (ROBINS-I). Los resultados se sintetizaron narrativamente y se realizó un metaanálisis donde se disponía de datos suficientes. De 492 estudios identificados, 2 NRSI (n = 49) cumplieron criterios de inclusión, ambos estaban en riesgo grave de sesgo. No existen ECA en diuréticos para la PAB-PH en lactantes prematuros. Mortalidad, resultados respiratorios, resultados de descarga y efectos adversos fueron reportados de manera inconsistente. Metaanálisis de datos limitados demostró pequeñas mejoras en marcadores ecocardiográficos, pero la certeza de evidencia fue muy baja debido a la heterogeneidad entre los dos estudios incluidos. Para concluir, evidencia que apoya el uso de diuréticos en la PAB-PH en bebés prematuros sigue siendo limitada y de poca certeza. Estudios de alta calidad son necesarios para definir mejor su seguridad y eficacia.

abstract_en: Low-load blood flow restriction resistance training (BFR-RT) may offer a lower-load alternative to conventional resistance training for older adults, but its cardiovascular responses and neuromuscular benefits remain incompletely characterized. To synthesize the acute cardiovascular responses and chronic cardiovascular and neuromuscular effects of low-load BFR-RT in older adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials, including parallel-group and crossover designs, comparing low-load BFR-RT with no-exercise/passive control or conventional non-BFR resistance training were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twenty-seven studies were included. Acutely, BFR-RT increased systolic blood pressure versus no exercise (MD, 5.30 mmHg; 95% CI, 0.48 to 10.12) and increased diastolic blood pressure (MD, 5.23 mmHg) and mean arterial pressure (MD, 5.81 mmHg) versus conventional resistance training, while heart rate, stroke volume, and cardiac output were not significantly different. Chronically, resting cardiovascular and endothelial outcomes were largely unchanged. Versus no exercise, BFR-RT significantly improved knee-extension, leg-extension, and leg-press 1RM and quadriceps cross-sectional area. Comparisons with conventional resistance training were mixed and outcome-specific. Low-load BFR-RT improves selected neuromuscular outcomes in older adults, particularly relative to no exercise, while cardiovascular responses are comparator-dependent and chronic vascular effects appear largely neutral. These findings support cautious, individualized application rather than assumptions of cardiovascular superiority or equivalence to conventional resistance training.

abstract_en:
Background
Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.Results
Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).Conclusion
LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

abstract_en: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

La psoriasis en placa moderada a grave se asocia con inflamación sistémica persistente y aumento del riesgo cardiovascular. Para evaluar la asociación entre la terapia anti-TNF y los resultados cardiovasculares clínicos en adultos con psoriasis en placa moderada a grave, los autores realizaron una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis de acuerdo con PRISMA 2020 y prospectivamente registraron el protocolo en PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Fueron elegibles ensayos controlados aleatorios y estudios observacionales comparativos que evaluaron la terapia anti-TNF frente a placebo, sin exposición a TNF, terapia tópica y/o fototerapia, o terapia sistémica no biológica. Los resultados de interés fueron Eventos Cardiovasculares Adversos Mayores (MACE), infarto de miocardio, accidente cerebrovascular, muerte cardiovascular, insuficiencia cardiaca, fibrilación auricular, tromboembolismo venoso y mortalidad por cualquier causa. Se incluyeron 14 estudios.En evidencia aleatoria, el tratamiento anti-TNF no se asoció con diferencias significativas en el riesgo de MACE, infarto de miocardio, accidente cerebrovascular o insuficiencia cardiaca.En análisis observacionales estratificados por comparador, el tratamiento anti-TNF se asoció con un menor riesgo agrupado de eventos cardiovasculares notificados frente a terapia tópica, pero no versus terapia oral o fototerapia. La evidencia disponible se vio limitada por un seguimiento corto en ensayos aleatorizados, bajos recuentos de eventos cardiovasculares, amplios intervalos de confianza y evaluación indirecta de los resultados cardiovasculares, ya que la mayoría de los ensayos fueron diseñados principalmente para la eficacia dermatológica y la seguridad general en lugar de las variables cardiovasculares. Los agentes anti-TNF no se asociaron con un claro aumento del riesgo cardiovascular mayor y parecen tener un perfil aceptable de seguridad cardiovascular a corto plazo. Sin embargo, la evidencia actual no establece un efecto cardioprotector concluyente, y se necesitan estudios prospectivos más amplios con un seguimiento más prolongado.

abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD. A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO2), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics. A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO2 (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO2 improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory. Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.

La enfermedad cardiovascular (CVD) sigue siendo la principal causa de muerte en todo el mundo, pero la participación en la rehabilitación cardíaca (CR) sigue siendo subóptima.Los wreables usados en muñecas pueden apoyar la RC completamente remota o híbrida mediante el monitoreo de actividad y la retroalimentación individualizada, pero la efectividad y la consistencia de los beneficios siguen siendo inciertas. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo evaluar la efectividad de la CR guiada por muñecas y desgastadas, entregada a través de programas totalmente remotos o híbridos iniciados durante la RC de fase II o III en pacientes con CVD. Se buscaron 8 bases de datos para ensayos controlados aleatorizados publicados desde el 1 de enero de 2015, hasta el 7 de agosto de 2026. Los ensayos elegibles incluyeron adultos con ECV e integraron una muñeca desgastada en RC totalmente remota o híbrida. Se excluyeron los estudios centrados principalmente en insuficiencia cardíaca o usando wearables solamente para la medición del resultado. Los resultados primarios fueron consumo máximo de oxígeno (VO2), distancia a pie de 6 minutos (6MWD) y pasos diarios. Los metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios utilizaron diferencias medias (MD), excepto para la calidad de vida, que utilizó MD estandarizados. Se estimó la varianza entre el estudio utilizando el método DerSimonian-Laird, IC de efecto agrupado utilizaron el ajuste Knapp-Hartung, y los intervalos de predicción del 95% (PI) usaron el método de la trampa paramétrica Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo con Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Los análisis de subgrupos y metarregresión univariable exploraron las características del estudio y de la intervención, se incluyeron 18 ensayos en los que participaron participantes aleatorizados de 1993, reportados en 20 publicaciones; 17 contribuyeron al metaanálisis; las estimaciones agrupadas favorecieron la CR guiada por el desgaste para el VO2 máximo (10 estudios; 591 participantes; MD 1,69; IC 95% 0,46-2,92,9; PI 95% -2,21 a 5,39 ml/kg/min), 6MWD (9 estudios; 1094 participantes; MD 31,03; IC 95% 7,66-53,92; PI 95% -62,11 a 123,18 m), y los pasos diarios (8 estudios; 474 participantes; MD 1062,8; IC 95% 383,5-1825,0; PI 95% -503,0 a 2860,0 pasos/día). Los 3 IPs incluyeron el nulo, lo que indica incertidumbre sobre la consistencia en futuros escenarios comparables. No se observaron efectos agrupados claros para umbral anaeróbico, IMC, circunferencia de la cintura, fuerza de agarre o calidad de vida. Las diferencias de subgrupo no fueron estadísticamente significativas.En metarregresión univariable, una mayor proporción de participantes femeninos se asoció con mayor mejoría del pico VO2, aunque este hallazgo de nivel agregado fue exploratorio. Sin embargo, los IPs incluyeron el nulo, lo que indica incertidumbre sobre la consistencia en futuros ajustes.Estos programas pueden extender el monitoreo de actividad, retroalimentación individualizada y apoyo conductual más allá de la RC basada en el centro, pero su naturaleza multicomponente evita atribuir efectos a los wearables solos.Los ensayos más grandes y rigurosamente diseñados con protocolos y resultados estandarizados deben identificar a los pacientes y componentes del programa más propensos a beneficiarse.

abstract_en: Sepsis causes deaths worldwide each day, with hemodynamic resuscitation being central to management. Guidelines recommend a 65-mm Hg mean arterial pressure (MAP) target, yet the evidence for elevated targets remains fragmented across mortality, renal, and splanchnic outcomes. This review aims to comprehensively appraise the impact of elevated MAP targets on splanchnic ischemia, mortality, and organ-specific outcomes in septic resuscitation. Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar for studies comparing MAP targets in septic shock. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; randomized controlled trials [RCTs]) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (nonrandomized studies). The findings were synthesized narratively according to the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guidelines, with random-effects meta-analysis for mortality outcomes. Evidence certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. From 3254 records, 11 studies (2895 patients; 4 RCTs, 7 nonrandomized) met the inclusion criteria. Pooled 90-day mortality across 3 trials showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality with elevated MAP targets (320/720, 44.4% vs 280/722, 38.8%; OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.97-1.77). Pooled 28- or 30-day mortality showed a similar nonsignificant trend (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.98-1.61), which was robust to sensitivity analysis. Narratively, mortality findings across nonpooled observational studies were inconsistent; some linked low MAP to higher death risk, and others found no significant association. Renal outcomes were inconsistent, with some studies showing reduced renal replacement therapy or improved acute kidney injury recovery at higher targets, particularly in hypertensive or cirrhotic subgroups. Elevated MAP targets consistently increased vasopressor exposure and were associated with more arrhythmias and fewer organ support-free days. No study reported splanchnic ischemia as a discrete outcome; mesenteric ischemia rates were low and similar between arms. Overall certainty of evidence was very low. Higher MAP targets show no clear mortality or splanchnic perfusion benefit and may increase overall harm, though select subgroups, chronic hypertension, and cirrhosis, may benefit, supporting individualized, risk-stratified MAP targeting over uniformly elevated-target strategies.

La sepsis causa muertes en todo el mundo cada día, siendo la reanimación hemodinámica central para el manejo. Las guías recomiendan un objetivo de presión arterial media (PAP) de 65 mm Hg, sin embargo la evidencia de metas elevadas permanece fragmentada a través de los resultados de mortalidad, renal y esplancínico. Esta revisión tiene como objetivo evaluar exhaustivamente el impacto de los objetivos de PAM elevados en la isquemia esplancónica, mortalidad y resultados específicos de órganos en la reanimación séptica. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando el Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; ensayos controlados aleatorios [RCTs]) y la Escala Newcastle-Ottawa (estudios no aleatorizados), cuyos hallazgos fueron sintetizados narrativamente de acuerdo con las directrices Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis, con metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios para los resultados de mortalidad. La certeza de la evidencia fue calificada utilizando el marco Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) de 3254 registros, 11 estudios (2895 pacientes; 4 ECRs, 7 no aleatorizados) cumplieron los criterios de inclusión. La mortalidad de 90 días agrupada en 3 ensayos mostró una tendencia no significativa hacia una mayor mortalidad con metas de PAM elevadas (320/720, 44,4% vs 280/722, 38,8%; OR 1,31, IC 95% 0,97-1,77). La mortalidad de 28 ó 30 días agrupada mostró una tendencia similar no significativa (OR 1,25, IC 95% 0,98-1,61), que fue robusta para el análisis de sensibilidad. Narrativamente, los hallazgos de mortalidad en los estudios observacionales no agrupados fueron inconsistentes; algunos vincularon una PAM baja a un mayor riesgo de muerte, y otros no encontraron asociación significativa. Los resultados renales fueron inconsistentes, con algunos estudios que mostraron reducción de la terapia de reemplazo renal o mejoría de la recuperación de la lesión renal aguda en metas más altas, particularmente en subgrupos hipertensos o cirróticos. Los objetivos de la PAM elevada aumentaron consistentemente la exposición vasopresora y se asociaron con más arritmias y menos días libres de soporte orgánico. Ningún estudio reportó isquemia esplancónica como resultado discreto; las tasas de isquemia mesentérica fueron bajas y similares entre los brazos. La certeza general de la evidencia fue muy baja. Los objetivos más altos de la PAM no muestran un beneficio claro de mortalidad o perfusión esplancónica y pueden aumentar el daño general, aunque determinados subgrupos, hipertensión crónica y cirrosis, pueden beneficiar, apoyando la focalización de la PAM individualizada y estratificada por riesgo sobre estrategias objetivo uniformemente elevadas.

abstract_en:
Aims
Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most.Methods
Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI.Primary outcomes
all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes.Results
Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes.Conclusions
SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

abstract_en: Randomized trials established the efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). We assessed whether their effectiveness in routine practice is concordant with trial efficacy, appraising and pooling each evidence stream separately. PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 1, 2015 to July 2026 for randomized trials and comparative observational studies of SGLT2 inhibitors vs. placebo or nonuse in adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40% reporting mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Adjusted all-cause mortality was pooled by random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment; other outcomes were synthesized narratively. Trial and observational estimates were never combined, and certainty was graded with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria. Eleven studies were included (two trials and nine observational). For all-cause mortality, the pooled observational HR (0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.79; I² = 0%) indicated a larger apparent benefit than the pooled trial estimate (HR 0.87, 0.77-0.98). In one registry, the association attenuated to borderline nonsignificance after adjustment for background therapy. For heart failure hospitalization, a consistent trial benefit (HR 0.69, 0.62-0.78) contrasted with attenuated or null real-world estimates (HR 0.84-1.03). Real-world mortality associations with SGLT2 inhibitors in HFrEF are directionally concordant with trial efficacy, but their larger magnitude most plausibly reflects residual confounding, including co-prescription of other guideline-directed therapy. Real-world hospitalization estimates diverged from trials, likely reflecting outcome ascertainment. With very low-certainty observational evidence, the trial estimate remains the best guide to causal benefit.
abstract_es: Abstract

Los ensayos aleatorizados establecieron la eficacia de los inhibidores del cotransportador de sodio-glucosa 2 (SGLT2) en la insuficiencia cardiaca con fracción de eyección reducida (HFrEF). Se evaluó si su eficacia en la práctica rutinaria es concordante con la eficacia del ensayo, evaluando y agrupando cada flujo de evidencia por separado. PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) y ClinicalTrials.gov fueron buscados entre el 1 de enero de 2015 y julio de 2026 para ensayos aleatorizados y estudios observacionales comparativos de inhibidores del SGLT2 frente a placebo o no uso en adultos con fracción de eyección ventricular izquierda ≤40% reportando mortalidad o hospitalización por insuficiencia cardiaca. El riesgo de sesgo fue evaluado con el Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 y la Escala Newcastle-Ottawa. La mortalidad por todas las causas ajustada fue agrupada por metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios con el ajuste Hartung-Knapp; otros resultados fueron sintetizados narrativamente. Las estimaciones de ensayos y observaciones nunca fueron combinadas, y la certeza fue calificada con el criterio Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) y se incluyeron once estudios (dos ensayos y nueve observacionales). Para la mortalidad por todas las causas, la FC observacional compartida (0,75, IC 95% 0,71-0,79; I2 = 0%) indicó un beneficio aparente mayor que la estimación del ensayo combinado (HR 0,87, 0,77-0,98). En un registro, la asociación atenuó a una no significancia límite después del ajuste para la terapia de fondo. Para la hospitalización por insuficiencia cardiaca, un beneficio consistente en el ensayo (HR 0,69, 0,62-0,78) contrastaba con estimaciones atenuadas o nulas en el mundo real (HR 0,84-1,03). Las asociaciones de mortalidad real con inhibidores SGLT2 en HFrEF son direccionalmente concordantes con la eficacia del ensayo, pero su mayor magnitud refleja de manera plausible la confusión residual, incluyendo la co-prescripción de otra terapia dirigida. Con pruebas observacionales de muy baja certeza, la estimación del ensayo sigue siendo la mejor guía para el beneficio causal.

title: Dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for pure native aortic regurgitation via transfemoral access: a meta-analysis of contemporary outcomes.

abstract_en:
Background
Pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR) poses unique technical challenges for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), including annular dilatation and absent calcification for anchoring. Whilst dedicated aortic regurgitation (AR) devices have been developed, their comparative performance against off-label devices specifically via transfemoral access - the contemporary standard approach - remains incompletely defined.Aims
We aimed to compare the outcomes of dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for PNAR via transfemoral access in contemporary practice.Methods
We systematically searched PubMed (MEDLINE) and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-November 2025) for studies reporting transfemoral TAVI outcomes in PNAR. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression was performed.Results
Twenty-four studies (2,956 patients) were included comprising 25 cohorts: 4 cohorts (537 patients) evaluated dedicated devices, and 21 cohorts (2,419 patients) assessed off-label devices. Overall, 30-day mortality was 3.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-4.8%). Dedicated devices showed a trend towards lower mortality (1.9% vs 4.1%, odds ratio [OR] 0.45, 95% CI: 0.20-1.00; p=0.051; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19-0.83). Dedicated devices achieved higher device success (95.8% vs 85.7%, OR 3.64; p=0.012), lower rates of residual AR >=moderate (0.6% vs 6.2%, OR 0.11; p=0.048), reduced valve embolisation (2.0% vs 7.3%, OR 0.26; p=0.048), and fewer reinterventions (2.0% vs 7.9%, OR 0.22; p=0.010). Permanent pacemaker implantation (20.8%), stroke (2.6%), and major bleeding (3.0%) were similar between groups.Conclusions
In contemporary transfemoral TAVI for PNAR, dedicated devices demonstrated superior procedural outcomes compared with off-label devices. These findings support the preferential use of dedicated devices in this population, though randomised trials are needed to establish definite treatment recommendations.

abstract_en: Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAA and AAA) progress silently, and no drug has been shown to slow their growth. Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA. Aneurysm growth was standardized to mm/year and pooled with random-effects models when at least three comparable studies were available. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE. Thirty-three studies were included, 32 observational and one randomized; fewer than 20% of participants were women. Circulating lipid fractions showed no consistent association with aneurysm growth. Statin use was associated with slower growth (mean difference -0.78 mm/year; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.43; I2 = 92.4%; 95% prediction interval -2.02 to 0.46 mm/year), lower all-cause mortality, and fewer aortic complications. In AAA, metformin use was associated with slower growth in observational studies (-0.34 mm/year; 95% CI -0.48 to -0.20; I2 = 46.3%), while the single randomized trial found no difference. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. In these largely observational data, aneurysm progression was more closely related to statin and metformin use than to circulating lipid levels, a pattern that is hypothesis-generating and from which causality cannot be inferred.
abstract_es: Abstract

Los aneurismas torácicos y aórticos abdominales (TAA y AAA) progresan silenciosamente, y no se ha demostrado que ningún fármaco retarde su crecimiento. Los lípidos circulantes, las estatinas y la metformina son modificadores de enfermedades candidatas, pero la evidencia es heterogénea y en gran medida observacional. Buscamos MEDLINE, Embase y la Biblioteca Cochrane desde el inicio hasta el 24 de marzo de 2025, con una actualización de MEDLINE hasta el 3 de octubre de 2026, para estudios aleatorizados y de cohortes de adultos con AAA o TAA establecidos. El crecimiento del aneurisma se estandarizó hasta mm/año y se reunió con modelos de efectos aleatorios cuando se disponía de al menos tres estudios comparables. Se incluyeron 33 estudios, 32 observacionales y uno aleatorizado; menos del 20% de los participantes fueron mujeres. Las fracciones lipídicas circulantes no mostraron asociación consistente con el crecimiento del aneurisma. El uso de estatinas se asoció con un crecimiento más lento (diferencia media -0,78 mm/año; IC 95% -1,13 a -0,43; I2 = 92,4%; intervalo de predicción 95% -2,02 a 0,46 mm/año), mortalidad por todas las causas más baja y menos complicaciones aórticas. En AAA, el uso de metformina se asoció con un crecimiento más lento en estudios observacionales (-0,34 mm/año; IC 95% -0,48 a -0,20; I2 = 46,3%), mientras que el ensayo aleatorizado único no encontró diferencia alguna. En estos datos, en gran medida observacionales, la progresión del aneurisma estuvo más estrechamente relacionada con el uso de estatinas y metformina que con los niveles de lípidos circulantes, un patrón que es generador de hipótesis y del cual no se puede inferir causalidad.

abstract_en: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. abstract_en:
Background
Inflammation and dysregulation of adipokines play key roles in the development of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Walnuts (Juglans regia L.), rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, fiber, and antioxidants, may modulate inflammatory and metabolic pathways; however, evidence from interventional studies remains inconsistent. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis aimed to determine the effects of walnut consumption on inflammatory cytokines and adipokines in adults.Methods
A comprehensive literature search was conducted in databases through July 2026 to identify relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of walnut intake on C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), adiponectin, and leptin. Weighted mean differences (WMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Subgroup, sensitivity, and non-linear dose-response analyses were performed.Results
The pooled analysis of 24 RCTs (2068 participants) showed that Walnut intake was associated with a small reduction in CRP concentrations (WMD: -1.0 mg/dL; 95% CI: -1.9 to -0.1; p = 0.031) and IL-6 concentrations (WMD: -0.11 pg/mL; 95% CI: -0.20, -0.01; p = 0.028). However, sensitivity analyses indicated that this finding was not robust to the exclusion of several influential studies. No significant effects were observed for TNF-α (WMD: 0.21 pg/mL, p = 0.306), adiponectin (WMD: -0.17 ng/mL, p = 0.678), or leptin (WMD: 1.39 ng/mL, p = 0.314). Subgroup analyses revealed more potent anti-inflammatory effects with interventions lasting more than 12 weeks and doses above 50 g/day.Conclusions
Walnut consumption may be associated with small reductions in CRP and IL-6 levels, without significant effects on TNF-α or adipokine concentrations. However, these effects are modest, and their clinical relevance remains uncertain.

abstract_en:
Background
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.Methods
A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.Results
Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.Conclusion
AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

abstract_en: A recent meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with cardiovascular adverse events (AEs) leading to treatment discontinuation in asthma, although the certainty of evidence was low. To evaluate the cardiovascular safety of long-acting bronchodilators in a real-world asthma population. This population-based cohort study used UK Biobank data from patients with asthma (2006-2010). Exposure was categorized into three mutually exclusive groups: LABA alone, LAMA alone, or combined LABA/LAMA therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular AEs, including coronary heart disease, arrhythmia, hypertension, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Pre-specified subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed. A total of 14,677 patients were included (median follow-up 14.68 years). Long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with an increased risk of total cardiovascular AEs (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.15). This was primarily driven by arrhythmia (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.42), heart failure (HR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02-1.65), and cerebrovascular disease (HR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). When stratified by regimen, the association was confined to the LABA group (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.001-1.13) and the combined group (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.09-1.59). The association was more pronounced in patients using short-acting bronchodilators (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.07-1.23; interaction P = 0.004). The observed positive associations are more plausibly attributable to confounding rather than to a causal drug effect. Future research should prioritize new-user designs to clarify whether these signals are drug-specific or confounded by disease severity.

Un reciente metaanálisis de ensayos controlados aleatorizados encontró que el uso de broncodilatadores de acción prolongada se asoció con eventos adversos cardiovasculares (AEs) que llevaron a la interrupción del tratamiento en asma, aunque la certeza de evidencia fue baja. Para evaluar la seguridad cardiovascular de broncodilatadores de acción prolongada en una población asmática real, este estudio de cohorte basado en la población utilizó datos de UK Biobank de pacientes con asma (2006-2010).La exposición se clasificó en tres grupos mutuamente excluyentes: LABA solo, LAMA solo o terapia combinada LABA/LAMA. El resultado primario fue un compuesto de EA cardiovasculares, incluyendo cardiopatía coronaria, arritmia, hipertensión, insuficiencia cardiaca y enfermedad cerebrovascular. Se utilizaron modelos de riesgos proporcionales de Cox para estimar las razones de riesgo (HR) con intervalos de confianza del 95% (IC). Se realizaron análisis de subgrupos preespecificados y pruebas de interacción. Se incluyó un total de 14.677 pacientes (mediana de seguimiento 14,68 años). El uso broncodilatador de acción prolongada se asoció con un aumento del riesgo de EA cardiovasculares totales (HR: 1,08, IC 95%: 1,02-1,15). Esto fue impulsado principalmente por arritmias (HR: 1,23, IC 95%: 1,06-1,42), insuficiencia cardiaca (HR: 1,30, IC 95%: 1,02-1,65), y enfermedad cerebrovascular (HR: 1,35, IC 95%: 1,02-1,79), cuando se estratificaron por régimen, la asociación se limitó al grupo LABA (HR: 1,07, IC 95%: 1,01-1,13) y al grupo combinado (HR: 1,32, IC 95%: 1,09-1,59). La asociación fue más pronunciada en pacientes que utilizaban broncodilatadores de acción corta (HR: 1,15, IC 95%: 1,07-1,23; interacción P = 0,004). Las asociaciones positivas observadas son más plausiblemente atribuibles a la confusión en lugar de a un efecto fármaco causal. Las investigaciones futuras deben priorizar los diseños de nuevos usuarios para aclarar si estas señales son específicas de los medicamentos o están confundidas por la gravedad de la enfermedad.

abstract_en: Lower gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic criteria on an oral glucose tolerance test are widely recommended, but their impacts on maternal, neonatal, long-term and economic outcomes remain uncertain. To compare outcomes after GDM diagnosis using lower versus higher diagnostic strategies. We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing outcomes following assessment for GDM and treatment if indicated, using lower versus higher glycemic diagnostic criteria or thresholds in four databases and four trial registries (PROSPERO registration CRD420251183179) to 27th July 2026. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias, conducted random-effects meta-analyses and evaluated GRADE certainty. Seventeen studies were included, with nine RCTs and one cohort study contributing to the meta-analysis (81,528 women). Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12 more), but had little to no effect on other short-term outcomes. Longer-term evidence was limited to follow-up of one RCT reporting reduced maternal hypertension and child neurodevelopmental impairment but increased subsequent GDM at five-year follow-up with use of lower criteria or thresholds. Findings on GDM-related healthcare costs were inconsistent, with no long-term economic data. Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.
abstract_es: Abstract

Se recomiendan ampliamente los criterios diagnósticos de diabetes gestacional inferior (GDM) en una prueba oral de tolerancia a la glucosa, pero sus impactos en los resultados maternos, neonatales, a largo plazo y económicos permanecen inciertos. Para comparar los resultados después del diagnóstico de GDM usando estrategias diagnósticas más bajas versus más altas. Se buscaron ensayos controlados aleatorizados (CRT) y estudios prospectivos de cohorte que comparan los resultados después de la evaluación de GDM y tratamiento si se indica, utilizando criterios diagnósticos o umbrales glucémicos más bajos versus más altos en cuatro bases de datos y cuatro registros de ensayos (registro PROSPERO CRD4202511831979) al 27 de julio de 2026. Dos revisores evaluaron de manera independiente el riesgo de sesgo, realizaron metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios y evaluaron la certeza de GRADE. Se incluyeron 17 estudios, con nueve ECA y un estudio de cohorte que contribuyeron al metaanálisis (81.528 mujeres). Criterios o umbrales diagnósticos más bajos, comparados con criterios o umbrales diagnósticos más altos, duplicaron el diagnóstico de GDM y el uso de farmacoterapia, aumentaron la hipoglucemia neonatal (RCT: 18 más por 1.000; IC 95% 11 a 25 más) y la separación materno-neonatal (RCT: 6 más por 1.000; IC 95% 1 a 12 más), pero tuvieron poco o ningún efecto en otros resultados a corto plazo. La evidencia a más largo plazo se limitó al seguimiento de una notificación de ECA que redujo la hipertensión materna y el deterioro del neurodesarrollo infantil, pero aumentó la DMG posterior en un seguimiento de cinco años con el uso de criterios o umbrales más bajos. Los hallazgos sobre los costos de atención médica relacionados con el DMA fueron inconsistentes, sin datos económicos a largo plazo. Los criterios diagnósticos más bajos aumentaron el diagnóstico de DMG y algunos aspectos de la utilización de la atención médica, sin mejorar los resultados a corto plazo.

abstract_en: ObjectiveAs healthcare systems increasingly emphasize value-based care, evidence regarding the economic implications of nonpharmacologic interventions is needed to inform implementation and reimbursement decisions. This study aimed to assess the economic value of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction, identify clinical populations in which economic evaluations have been conducted, and assess the strength of the available economic evidence.DesignSystematic review of economic evaluations.Setting and ParticipantsAll clinical populations and healthcare settings. InterventionsMindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).Evidence Review MethodsThis systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses 2020 guidelines and was prospectively registered. Nine databases, including MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus, were searched from inception through March 2026 without language restriction, with reference-list screening and citation tracking. Eligible studies evaluated Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction and at least one economic outcome. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Quality of Health Economic Studies instrument and the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 checklist.ResultsAmong 468 identified records, 12 economic evaluations met inclusion criteria. Studies included 8 randomized clinical trials, 2 Markov models, and 2 prospective cohort studies, conducted in North America (6) and Europe (6). Chronic pain conditions were most frequent (6), followed by mental health disorders (3), breast cancer survivorship (2), and pulmonary arterial hypertension (1). Across these populations, reductions in healthcare utilization and productivity losses generally offset delivery costs, resulting in lower overall costs with equivalent or improved health outcomes for Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction compared with treatment-as-usual. Results were also favorable or comparable relative to active comparators including cognitive behavioral therapy. Despite intervention costs of $195 to $866 per participant (mean, $461), all cost-utility analyses comparing Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction with treatment-as-usual over at least 6 months reported lower costs with equivalent or improved outcomes. Methodological quality was high, with 10 of 12 studies meeting above 80% quality criteria and 5 achieving 100% adherence. Reporting transparency was generally strong.ConclusionsMindfulness-Based Stress Reduction was associated with favorable economic outcomes across chronic pain, mental health, and breast cancer survivorship populations. Current evidence suggests that MBSR may represent a high-value nonpharmacologic intervention, with reductions in healthcare utilization and productivity losses frequently offsetting intervention costs. Additional economic evaluations are needed in underrepresented populations, healthcare settings, and delivery models.

Nueve bases de datos, incluyendo MEDLINE, Embase y Scopus, fueron buscadas desde el inicio hasta marzo de 2026 sin restricción de lenguaje, con revisión de lista de referencia y seguimiento de citas. Dos revisores revisaron independientemente los registros, extrajeron datos y evaluaron la calidad utilizando el instrumento de Estudios Económicos de Calidad de la Salud y la lista de verificación de las Normas de Evaluación Económica de la Salud 2022.ResultadosEntre los 468 registros identificados, 12 evaluaciones económicas cumplieron criterios de inclusión.Los estudios incluyeron 8 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados, 2 modelos Markov y 2 estudios prospectivos de cohortes, realizados en América del Norte (6) y Europa (6).Las condiciones de dolor crónico fueron más frecuentes (6), seguidas de trastornos de salud mental (3), supervivencia del cáncer de mama (2) e hipertensión arterial pulmonar (1). Los resultados también fueron favorables o comparables en relación con los comparadores activos, incluida la terapia cognitiva conductual. A pesar de los costos de intervención de $195 a $866 por participante (media, $461), todos los análisis de costo-utilidad que comparan la reducción del estrés basado en la atención de la conciencia con el tratamiento habitual durante al menos 6 meses reportaron menores costos con resultados equivalentes o mejorados. abstract_en: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the principal target for preventing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet many patients do not reach treatment goals with statins, and established proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) antibodies require injections every 2-4 weeks. Recaticimab is a humanized anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibody designed for dosing intervals of up to 12 weeks. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to March 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing recaticimab with placebo in adults with dyslipidemia. Four double-blind trials (1657 randomized participants) were included. At week 12, recaticimab reduced LDL-C by 47.31 percentage points relative to placebo (95% confidence interval [CI], -49.87 to -44.75; I2 = 0%), with similar reductions for 150 mg every 4 weeks (-49.63), 300 mg every 8 weeks (-49.43), and 450 mg every 12 weeks (-45.50) (P for subgroup difference = 0.29).
